Morning briefing in 3 commands: jarvis init --preset morning-digest-mac --force   (or -linux / -minimal) jarvis connect gdrive   (one Google sign-in covers Gmail, Calendar, Tasks) jarvis digest --fresh   (or just say "good morning" in the chat) If jarvis isn't found, put uv run in front of it. Heads up: - The spoken briefing uses a Cartesia or OpenAI API key (paid). Free: jarvis digest --text-only to read it (a local open source Kokoro voice is also in the code). - Gmail needs your own Google OAuth client (client_id:client_secret), the docs walk you through it. - Models run locally through Ollama, so your computer has to handle a local model. Cloud models are optional. - The installer asks about anonymous analytics - answer N if you don't want it. - The 40 emails in the video are an example, not a test result. No code words - everything's right here. Follow arti.miller - next I'll play you the first real briefing my Jarvis gives me.

AI video editor in Claude Code: 3 free prompts, from an empty folder to a finished reel. #claudecode #videoediting #aitools #reels #claude SETUP (once) 1. Get the Claude app (claude.ai/download) and open the Code tab, not the browser. 2. Make a folder "AI Editor" with 3 folders inside: raw, references, done. 3. New chat in Code, choose Local, select the AI Editor folder. Needs a paid Claude plan. Runs on a computer, not a phone. PROMPT 1: TOOLS You're my video editor. We work in this folder: raw, references, done. Install and verify 5 tools: FFmpeg with libass (on Mac: ffmpeg-full, full path), faster-whisper for word-level subtitles, yt-dlp for references, Remotion, HyperFrames (npm package hyperframes). Check what's installed first. Official installs only (Homebrew, winget, npm/pip), Node.js 22+. Python packages go in a .venv here: pip install faster-whisper "av<19". Test each for real: burn a subtitle into a test clip, transcribe 5 seconds of audio. Show a table: tool, version, works or not. PROMPT 2: YOUR TASTE Here are reels whose editing I like: [link 1] [link 2] [link 3]. My format: [talking to camera / voiceover]. Download them with yt-dlp into references (for study only). Study each one frame by frame and by ear: pacing, shot length, pause cuts, subtitles, colors, graphics, transitions, music, the first 3 seconds. Take inspiration, but don't copy: no shots, text, logos or brand elements. Write my own style to style.md with exact values. Show it to me. PROMPT 3: EDIT My new recording is in raw. Edit it using style.md: 1. Transcribe with Whisper, word timestamps. Ask me about doubtful words before burning subtitles. 2. Cut pauses, slips and bad takes, keep the last good take. Keep pauses that serve the meaning. Don't speed up my voice. 3. Word-by-word subtitles in my style. 4. If references/music.mp3 exists, put it quietly under the voice. 5. Graphics only where they help. 6. Export 1080x1920 to done as draft-v1.mp4 plus edit-notes.md. Check the file, then show me. Save my fixes as draft-v2, draft-v3. No code words - everything's right here. Follow arti.miller for a free Claude setup like this every day.

videos.caption: Hit follow and share your most UNHINGED tip! Automation comes last, not first. Asking AI for an answer is stage 1. The work gets more useful when you use AI to test ideas, learn your process, and handle bigger jobs with clear rules. The 5 stages: 1. Ask AI: Get an answer. 2. Think with AI: Find gaps in your ideas. 3. Teach AI: Show it how you like work done. 4. Delegate to AI: Give it a meaningful assignment. 5. Automate with AI: Have it repeat the work on a schedule. At stage 2, ask AI to find blind spots and question whether the work needs to exist. At stage 3, give AI context, examples, rules, and feedback. Let it ask questions. Check the output, then save your process as a reusable skill. At stage 4, give AI a real job with several files. Check every figure and piece of evidence before you trust the result. At stage 5, schedule a reliable skill. Start with drafts for human review. Add tools or connectors when the job needs fresh data.
